subject: Pricing exhibit erratum: margin reconciliation & packaging impact
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Chris Wolff <chris.wolff@atlashealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit erratum: margin reconciliation & packaging impact

Chris / Elena —

Thanks for the quick read-through yesterday. We dug into the pricing exhibit and found a margin/volume mapping erratum that changes how the floor & cap bands apply when the customer activates SKU-level packaging (bundle vs individual SKUs). We attach a redline that highlights the change (Atlas_Pricing_Redline_20260531.pdf).

High-level: the original exhibit assumed a blended effective rate per token across all SKUs. With the packaging option enabled, usage will be reported per SKU and the floor/cap calculations need to be scoped to the SKU family or else Atlas could be exposed to unintended overcharge/under-commit true-ups.

Questions we want to confirm with you before legal marks this up:
- Do you want floor/cap measured at the family level (recommended) or at the account-level aggregated across families?
- If measured at family level, do you expect auto-crediting if family volume falls below the stated floor on a quarterly true-up?
- Any internal procurement constraints on introducing a short-term stabilization credit (one-time bucket) vs. an ongoing entitlement?

Proposed next steps: you and Elena review the attached annotated exhibit and tell us if family-level measurement is acceptable. If yes, we’ll prepare a redline to the orderform that adds a "Family Floor/Ceiling Measurement" paragraph and an operational definition for SKU families.

FWIW from ops: switching to family-level measurement reduces billing volatility for customers that experiment with packaging, and it aligns with how our telemetry aggregates usage today.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week to walk through.

—David

David Kim
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 9:12 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Chris / Elena —
> 
> Thanks for the quick read-through yesterday....

Thanks, David. We got the redline and the annotated notes — appreciate the flag. A couple of clarifications from our side after reviewing with procurement: 

1) Atlas preference is account-level aggregation by default because we allocate spend to program-level budgets, not SKU families. Family-level measurement introduces reconciliation complexity for our internal chargeback.
2) If we must move to family-level measurement, procurement will insist on an auto-credit/true-up mechanism for any family that falls below the floor in a given quarter (i.e., if family usage < floor, Atlas receives a credit equal to the shortfall multiplied by the blended rate). We need this automated — manual credits will create too much overhead.
3) Packaging: when we enable a bundled SKU we expect the price per bundle to be additive (not discounting) unless explicitly included in the orderform pricing table. We cannot accept implicit discounts unless spelled out.

We can accept a compromise: keep account-level measurement in the orderform but carve out a definition that if the customer elects per-family metering (explicit checkbox on provisioning) then family-level rules and auto-credit true-ups apply. That preserves our billing model while giving customers an opt-in.

Would be great to get a redline from legal that implements the opt-in checkbox approach and a short description of the automation/ops contract (how credits are applied and timing).

Thanks —
Chris Wolff
Sr. Director Procurement | Atlas Health

Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit erratum: margin reconciliation & packaging impact

Looping in Karthik / legal ops to propose language and confirm implementation.

Karthik — can you please draft two short clauses:
1) An "Opt-in Family Metering" checkbox paragraph that, when checked at provisioning, switches floor/cap measurement to SKU-family scope and triggers the auto-credit true-up process described below.
2) A brief operational "Auto-Credit True-Up" clause that defines timing (quarterly true-up within 30 days of quarter close), calculation (shortfall * blended rate at family level), and a cap on credits (e.g., credits cannot exceed 20% of that quarter's billed amount to prevent gaming).

Also: Ops needs to confirm the automation surface — David, can you confirm which billing system endpoint we will call to post credits and whether we need an initial manual run for the first quarter? If automation is not in place by go-live, we should include a one-time stabilization credit instead of an ongoing true-up.

Chris / Elena — we will produce the two alternative paragraphs (opt-in family metering + fallback one-time stabilization credit) so you can choose which path to accept.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit erratum: margin reconciliation & packaging impact

Chris / Elena —

Thanks for the clear preference. We’ll do the opt-in family metering checkbox approach as the primary path and include the fallback one-time stabilization credit language if automation cannot be validated before go-live. Karthik — please draft the two clauses and include the 20% credit ceiling language Laura suggested.

Operational commitments (for clarity):
- If opt-in is selected, our billing will run a quarterly family-level reconciliation. Shortfalls will be credited at the blended family rate within 30 days of quarter close.
- If automation isn’t ready, Redwood will apply a one-time stabilization credit within 45 days of go-live, equal to the estimated first-quarter shortfall up to the 20% cap.

Chris — can you confirm Atlas is comfortable accepting the opt-in checkbox + automation definition? If yes, I’ll have legal prepare the redline to the orderform and route for execution. Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

Best —
David
